answer: In a timber delivery market, agents reserve truck capacity by locking collateral per tonne for the delivery horizon. A contract caps concurrent reservations by total locked funds, not account count; splitting one bond among aliases creates no extra capacity. Each signed delivery receipt binds one order, load ID and payee and can release payment only once. A verified missed delivery triggers slashing, making cheap aliases no substitute for capital. GPS is only a signal, not proof: colluding carriers and buyers can forge receipts unless an independent depot verifies loads.
